title: Valley Hall viscosity in the integer quantum Hall phases of (2+1)D Dirac materials
abstract: We calculate the valley-resolved Hall viscosity for Lorentz-invariant integer quantum Hall phases in Semenoff-semiconducting graphene-like systems at zero temperature. The Kubo formalism based discussion reported in Phys. Rev. B 100, 115421 (2019) revealed the divergence of single valley viscous Hall contributions for this case with only a valley-summed Hall viscosity being finite and therefore well-defined. Our approach to the Hall viscosity calculation is based on an equivalent Green function formulation within Wigner-Weyl calculus. We find that the previously identified divergence seems to be regularized to a finite value in a proper representation of the valley-resolved Hall viscosity in terms of energy eigenfunctions and eigenvalues. Together with the local Hall conductivity and its first nonlocal correction, reported as well in Phys. Rev. B 100, 115421 (2019), we extend the empirical relativistic Hoyos-Son formula to individual valleys. Both the original Hoyos-Son formula for Galilean invariant fluids and its relativistic extension to Dirac materials are found to be structurally identical for integer quantum Hall phases and expressible in terms of local electric and viscous Hall responses. In addition we evaluate the valley(-difference) Hall viscosity for biased Bernal bilayer graphene in the chiral fermion low energy approximation. Prospects of measuring valley Hall viscosity in nonlocal transport for mono- and bilayer graphene- and group-VI TMD-based devices are discussed.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the valley-resolved Hall viscosity in quantum Hall phases of 2D Dirac materials. It refines previous calculations by regularizing divergences and extends the Hoyos-Son relation to individual valleys. The work provides crucial insights into how viscous transport coefficients can be related to topological invariants in these advanced electronic systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is calculating the valley-resolved Hall viscosity ($\eta_{xy}^v$) for integer quantum Hall phases in (2+1)D Dirac materials.
main_result: The authors show that previous divergences in single-valley viscous contributions are regularized to finite values, and they extend the Hoyos-Son formula structure to individual valleys.
method: Calculations utilize an equivalent Green function formulation within Wigner-Weyl calculus and linear response theory applied to stress tensors.
model_or_system: The study focuses on (2+1)D Dirac materials, including graphene and TMDs, operating in the integer quantum Hall regime. Specific models include biased Bernal bilayer graphene for detailed analysis.
key_observables: Valley-resolved Hall viscosity ($\eta_{xy}^v$), local/nonlocal Hall conductivity ($\sigma_H(k)$), and the valley-$	ext{difference}$ Hall viscosity coefficient ($\eta_d$).
important_parameters: Filling factor ($p$), magnetic field ($B$), interlayer tunneling parameter ($\gamma_1$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on extending formulas derived for Lorentz-invariant systems, even when the specific low-energy model (like bilayer graphene) breaks these symmetries.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; the structure suggests derivations of explicit formulas for $\eta_s(p)$ and $\eta_d$ based on filling factor $p$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general formalism (Wigner-Weyl calculus, Hoyos-Son extension) to specific calculations for valley-summed and valley-difference viscosities in various Dirac systems.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous derivation of topological relations like the generalized Hoyos-Son formula connects macroscopic response coefficients (viscosity, conductivity) via fundamental symmetries, which has parallels in effective field theories used in AMO physics.
